blocks.text: # When an AI agent inherits yesterday's work, how does it know it is still valid?

**A technical write-up of Proofpress knowledge-handoff early testing**  
**Status:** complete early-testing report, 2026-08-12. The results below are bounded mechanism evidence from fixed GitHub Docs fixtures, not a general product-efficacy or benchmark claim.
## The problem is not just memory

Long-running agent work rarely stays inside one context window. A successor agent may receive the current files but not the predecessor's reasoning, or it may receive a good handoff after the underlying artifact has changed. These are different failures. The first creates **knowledge handoff debt**: the successor repeats already completed discovery and decision work. The second creates **stale inheritance risk**: the successor confidently reuses a decision that was valid for an older artifact revision.

Proofpress is designed around a simple distinction. A structured handoff carries semantic continuity: reviewed facts, accepted decisions, rejected routes, evidence references, open questions, and next actions. A version-bound handoff adds an independently executable check of the admitted artifact revision and a map of which inherited claims are affected when the current bytes differ. The expected benefit is therefore conditional, not universal: ordinary handoff should help when nothing changed; binding should matter when the artifact changed in a decision-relevant way.
## What we tested

We ran two complementary tracks using fixed public GitHub Docs revision pairs. Track 1 asked whether handing off prior work reduces rediscovery. Track 2 held the semantic handoff fixed and asked whether executable version binding changes the successor's response to artifact drift.

| Track | Arm | What the successor received |
|---|---|---|
| Knowledge handoff debt | H0 | Current artifact only |
| Knowledge handoff debt | H1 | Current artifact plus a natural prose handoff |
| Knowledge handoff debt | H2 | Current artifact plus a strong structured handoff |
| Version-bound handoff | V0 | Strong structured handoff with readable revision descriptions but no executable binding check |
| Version-bound handoff | V1 | The same semantic handoff plus admitted revision, lineage, native verification helper, and affected-claim map |

Track 1 used three unchanged-artifact fixtures: an alert-style revision, a how-to-structure revision, and a versioning-guidance revision. Track 2 used six fixtures: three irrelevant edits that changed bytes without affecting the inherited decision, and three relevant edits that narrowed supported Dependabot commands, retracted a legacy Copilot metrics API, or widened documented license-management permissions.

The primary DeepSeek receiver was OpenCode through Vercel AI Gateway to exact `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731`, with DeepInfra set as both the only and ordered provider and fallback disabled. The earlier mechanism calibration used the same harness and router with exact `zai/glm-5.2` and Z.AI-only routing. Per-call proxy telemetry was reconciled for the valid DeepSeek runs; all calls returned HTTP 200, resolved to the requested model and provider, and showed no fallback or cross-provider retry.
## Result 1: a handoff prevented visible rediscovery, but structure did not yet beat prose

All nine DeepSeek Track 1 responses were valid: three fixtures crossed with H0, H1, and H2. Every arm completed with the expected `proceed` disposition. The deterministic event scorer found one predefined source-rediscovery event in every H0 cell and none in either handoff arm.

| Track 1 arm | Valid responses | Fixtures with a rediscovery event |
|---|---:|---:|
| H0: artifact only | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| H1: natural prose handoff | 3/3 | 0/3 |
| H2: strong structured handoff | 3/3 | 0/3 |

The useful conclusion is modest but practical: in these three tasks, giving the successor a handoff avoided an observable source-read that the artifact-only successor used to reconstruct prior work. The experiment does **not** show that H2 outperformed H1. Both handoff formats carried enough information for these simple unchanged-artifact tasks, so the incremental value of stronger organization remains unresolved.
## Result 2: version binding produced the intended two-state behavior with GLM 5.2

The repaired GLM 5.2 Track 2 evidence contains 12 valid V0/V1 responses across the six fixtures. V1 ran the native binding helper in every fixture. It proceeded on all three irrelevant edits and targeted revalidation on all three relevant edits. V0 also proceeded on every irrelevant edit, but it continued on two of the three relevant edits; it independently noticed the direct Dependabot body conflict in the remaining fixture.

| GLM 5.2 state | V0 observed | V1 observed |
|---|---:|---:|
| Irrelevant edit | `proceed` 3/3 | `proceed` 3/3 |
| Relevant edit | `proceed` 2/3; `targeted_revalidate` 1/3 | `targeted_revalidate` 3/3 |

This was a repaired diagnostic rather than a clean first-pass run. The original V1 materialization omitted the required checkpoint, so all six V1 cells were isolated and rerun after the fixture repair. One timed-out V0 Dependabot cell was rerun separately. The repaired V1 report and the missing V0 retry, combined with the five unaffected original V0 cells, form the canonical 12-response result; the defective V1 cells and timed-out attempt are not treated as evidence.
## Result 3: DeepSeek reproduced the Track 2 aggregate pattern

DeepSeek then ran the same six-fixture V0/V1 comparison. All 12 responses were valid. V1 again proceeded on all three irrelevant edits and targeted revalidation on all three relevant edits. V0 again continued on two of the three relevant edits, although this time it independently detected the Copilot API conflict rather than the Dependabot conflict.

| DeepSeek state | V0 observed | V1 observed |
|---|---:|---:|
| Irrelevant edit | `proceed` 3/3 | `proceed` 3/3 |
| Relevant edit | `proceed` 2/3; `targeted_revalidate` 1/3 | `targeted_revalidate` 3/3 |

The model-level totals are repetitions over the same fixtures, so they are not 12 independent tasks. Descriptively, across both receivers V1 correctly proceeded on 6/6 irrelevant-edit responses and targeted revalidation on 6/6 relevant-edit responses. V0 proceeded on 6/6 irrelevant-edit responses but also proceeded on 4/6 relevant-edit responses. The fact that GLM and DeepSeek spontaneously caught different V0 conflicts is itself informative: readable prose sometimes enables self-correction, but which conflict gets noticed is not stable. The executable binding plus affected-claim path made the disposition stable on this fixture set.
## What the mechanism appears to be doing

The result is not “hash mismatch means stop.” Every V1 fixture had a revision mismatch. For irrelevant edits, the native helper established that the present artifact was the declared current revision, and the affected-claim map was empty, so the successor proceeded. For relevant edits, the same check established a valid current carrier while the impact map identified inherited claims whose basis had changed, so the successor revalidated only those claims. The observed behavior was selective admission: proceed through harmless drift, reopen affected work under relevant drift.

That distinction matters for product design. A system that merely warns whenever bytes change will create alert fatigue and false stops. A system that merely writes a better summary can still leave the successor guessing whether the summary belongs to the artifact in front of it. The early result suggests that semantic handoff and version binding solve separate parts of the continuity problem.
## What failed during the study, and why it matters

Several early runs were preserved but excluded. Besides the missing GLM V1 checkpoint and one V0 timeout, early DeepSeek Track 1 attempts exposed an overlong Gateway correlation value that produced HTTP 400 responses. The runner was changed to retain the human-readable run label while sending a deterministic short correlation key, and only the resulting r4 runs enter the reported nine-response denominator. These repairs are protocol evidence, not favorable outcomes silently pooled into the results.

The DeepSeek Track 1 Gateway aggregate endpoint also lagged the local call ledger by one or two calls for each run. We therefore use the immutable per-call reconciliation as the routing validity source and treat the eventually consistent aggregate report as corroboration, not as a substitute. The three Track 1 reconciliations cover 18, 23, and 20 local calls; the Track 2 reconciliation covers 82. These are tool-loop API calls, not independent experimental responses.
## What we can say now

The strongest supported product statement is: **in fixed GitHub Docs early tests, a handoff reduced visible rediscovery relative to artifacts alone, and adding Proofpress version binding plus affected-claim information made two different receiver models consistently distinguish harmless revision drift from decision-relevant drift.**

For a short public version: **“We tested whether an AI agent could safely inherit work after the underlying document changed. Across two receiver models on six fixed revision fixtures, the Proofpress-bound handoff proceeded on 6/6 harmless changes and selectively revalidated 6/6 decision-relevant changes. An unbound but equally detailed handoff proceeded on 4/6 relevant changes. In a separate three-fixture test, either prose or structured handoff avoided rediscovery seen with artifacts alone.”**
## What we cannot say yet

These fixtures use real public document revisions, but their experimental selection, handoffs, and state labels were produced by the originating team. Track 1 has only three unchanged tasks. Track 2 covers only irrelevant and relevant edits, not unchanged admission, authorized rollback, fork/merge ambiguity, mixed-version packages, or corrupt lineage. Each model contributed one response per cell. The reported results therefore do not establish a population effect size, statistical significance, real-world fault prevalence, or general superiority over ordinary handoffs.

The formal-gate audit passed package and scorer qualification but correctly set `formal_eligible=false` because the calibration fixtures were agent-authored and the state variants were constructed. Blind semantic judging and human audit were not completed for the reported DeepSeek Track 1 diagnostic. That does not invalidate the early product demonstration; it defines the boundary between a transparent technical blog and a formal external-efficacy claim.
## Where this goes next

The immediate product use is a public early-evidence release with the exact denominators, a small demo of the native binding decision, and links to the method and results. Stronger validation can then add independently authored fixtures, the remaining five artifact states, repeated receiver runs, recovery-cost measurement, and condition-blind review. Those additions would support a broader claim, but they are not prerequisites for sharing the bounded result above.
